reason: The hypothesis directly restates the well-known contrast between Al/Si (protective) and Mn (non-protective) oxidation behavior in CrFeCoNi-based HEAs, as reported in P1, P8, P33, and P36, without combining findings from different papers, transferring to a new regime, or proposing a novel mechanism. The core idea is a textbook-level summary of existing results.
copied_elements: Systematic variation of X (Al, Si, Mn) in CrFeCoNiX
Al or Si form protective oxides, Mn forms non-protective oxides
Mn leads to rapid cation diffusion and volatile oxide formation
Al2O3 and SiO2 are slow-growing, dense, adherent barrier layers
Mn-containing alloys develop thick, porous, spall-prone oxide scales
CrFeCoNiMn as baseline with unstable oxides
Competition between cation diffusion and oxygen ingress controls behavior
